A_target.statement:
In typed [[Definition:Combinatory Logic|combinatory logic]] with:
:$\mathsf K : A \to B \to A, \quad \mathsf S : \paren {A \to B \to C} \to \paren {A \to B} \to A \to C$
and application, a type is inhabited by a closed combinator term {{iff}} it is a theorem of implicational intuitionistic logic.

B_source.statement: The [[Definition:Hilbert Proof System|Hilbert system]] with axiom schemes $A \to \paren {B \to A}$ and $\paren {A \to \paren {B \to C} } \to \paren {\paren {A \to B} \to \paren {A \to C} }$ and modus ponens proves exactly the implicational intuitionistic tautologies, and satisfies the [[Deduction Theorem]].

object_map.reformulation: Transport Hilbert-style proofs to combinator terms, as natural deduction transports to lambda terms.

validity_conditions: Bracket abstraction removes a variable from a combinator term exactly as the deduction theorem removes a hypothesis.
The identity combinator I = S K K corresponds to the derivation of A -> A.
proof_plan: Assign to each instance of the two axiom schemes the combinators $\mathsf K$ and $\mathsf S$ of the same types, and to modus ponens the typing rule for application.
By induction on derivations, each Hilbert derivation of $\phi$ yields a closed combinator term of type $\phi$, and conversely each such term reads as a derivation.

The deduction theorem corresponds to bracket abstraction: $\sqbrk x x = \mathsf S \mathsf K \mathsf K$, $\sqbrk x u = \mathsf K \, u$ if $x$ is not free in $u$, and $\sqbrk x {u \, v} = \mathsf S \paren {\sqbrk x u} \paren {\sqbrk x v}$.

Hence inhabited types are exactly the theorems, which is the [[Definition:Curry-Howard Correspondence|Curry-Howard correspondence]] for Hilbert systems.
{{qed}}
